text:
mike: Heads-up — MosaicHealth just hit us with a concentrated 3min window of 429s around 00:31 UTC during their nightly claims job. They say the job fanouts ~1200 tiny requests concurrently. Getting this ticket now from their ops.

devon: Got logs? any rate-limit headers in responses? :eyes:

mike: Pasted what they sent below. They included a few response headers and a short curl test.

mike: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2025 00:31:12 GMT
x-rate-limit-limit: 600 RPM
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 24
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "Requests per minute quota exceeded"
}
```

mike: curl they ran:

mike: ```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-..." \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-lite","input":"ping"}' \\
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

tara: That `x-rate-limit-limit: 600 RPM` smells like a token-level per-minute cap from hosted plan (or org default). If they fanout 1200 reqs over 3 minutes, sustained bursts will definitely spike per-minute. Their pattern ~> 400 req/min for 3m.

devon: Two quick mitigations to suggest to Mosaic:
- combine/aggregate requests on client side (send larger batches) or use our batch endpoint if they have it
- add jittered exponential backoff (start 1s, cap 8s) and respect `Retry-After` header

jean: I'll ask them for account id and exact timestamps + example request IDs so we can cross-ref logs. If they want availability during the window we can propose a short dedicated capacity trial or request a transient quota bump while they refactor.

sre-bot: alert: ratecap-spike detected for account mosaic-health at 2051234567-2051234580, peaks: 480 req/min, 4.2k tokens/min, devices: mobile-sdk-v2

mike: Customer says they use our mobile SDK with default concurrency and their job submits ~1200 child requests (one per claim) rather than using server-side aggregation. They pushed a quick client change that reduced parallelism from 1200 -> 50 and the 429s stopped.

tara: Good signal that client-side fanout was root cause. For followups:
- Recommend: upgrade to batch endpoint or use server-side queue; mobile SDK has `max_concurrency` config — set to 20-50 for nightly batches
- Recommend: smooth ramp (throttle window) — e.g., rate 10 qps over 3m vs full fanout
- Offer: we can whitelist/raise RPM for a maintenance window if they need immediate relief while fixing.

devon: Also confirm whether they were hitting a project-level aggregate TPM cap (per-minute vs per-second confusion). Ask them to capture `x-rate-limit-*` headers on a few responses and forward.

jean: I've opened a support case (CASE-98732) and asked them to attach a minidump (timestamps + request-ids). I offered the temporary quota bump option and docs for SDK throttling examples.

mike: Action items:
- jean: collect account id + request-ids (done)
- tara: check tenant logs for cross-check + confirm whether this account has historical short windows of burst (slo deviation) — ETA 30m
- devon: draft an SDK guidance snippet for batching + config change we can paste to them

tara: Confirmed in logs: same token hit per-minute cap repeatedly, no backend errors. No infra issue on our side. Will post a short note in the ticket.

devon: Draft for SDK guidance:

devon: ```js
// mobile sdk: limit parallel requests for large fanouts
const client = new Redwood({ key: process.env.RWD_KEY, maxConcurrency: 40 });
// batch claims into groups of 25
await client.batchGenerate(claimsArray.chunk(25));
```

mike: Customer accepted the guidance, rolled out the concurrency cap, and will schedule a follow-up to explore a short dedicated capacity pilot. Closing on Slack once we confirm 24h of clean metrics. :thumbsup:

jean: I'll update CASE-98732 with the resolution and mark as support-provided guidance. If they request a quota bump, route to sales for dedicated sizing.

mike: Thanks everyone — flagging for postmortem-style doc if this repeats across >2 customers in next month. :white_check_mark:
